flyers-gate.definition: a door in a fence or wall, often outside
flyers-gate.hint: Close the gate so pets cannot run onto the road.
flyers-gate.fact: Airports also have 'gates' where you get on your plane.

flyers-geography.definition: the school subject about countries, land, and maps
flyers-geography.hint: In geography, you learn about mountains, rivers, and countries.
flyers-geography.fact: Geography helps you understand maps of the whole world.

flyers-get-to.hint: Ask 'How do I get to the station?' for directions.
flyers-get-to.fact: 'Get to' is another way of saying 'arrive at'.

flyers-glove.definition: clothing that covers and warms your hand
flyers-glove.hint: Wear gloves to keep your hands warm in winter.
flyers-glove.fact: Gloves have a separate space for each finger and thumb.

flyers-glue.definition: a sticky liquid used to join things together
flyers-glue.hint: Use glue to stick paper shapes in art class.
flyers-glue.fact: Glue can be made from plants, animals, or chemicals.

flyers-go-out.definition: to leave your home to do something
flyers-go-out.hint: We go out to play when the sun is shining.
flyers-go-out.fact: 'Go out' can also mean a light or fire stops burning.

flyers-gold.definition: having the colour of the shiny yellow metal gold
flyers-gold.hint: The winner's medal is often gold.
flyers-gold.fact: Real gold never rusts, even after thousands of years.

flyers-golf.definition: a game where you hit a small ball into holes
flyers-golf.hint: You use a long stick called a club to play golf.
flyers-golf.fact: Golf is usually played outside on a large, grassy course.

flyers-group.definition: a number of people or things together
flyers-group.hint: Work in a group of three for this activity.
flyers-group.fact: Animals like wolves also live and hunt in groups.

flyers-guess.definition: an answer you give without being completely sure
flyers-guess.hint: Have a guess even if you are not certain of the answer.
flyers-guess.fact: A good guess uses clues to make a smart choice.

flyers-gym.definition: a room or building with equipment for exercise
flyers-gym.hint: You do sport and exercise in the school gym.

flyers-half.definition: one of two equal parts of something
flyers-half.hint: Cut the apple in half to share it with a friend.
flyers-half.fact: Two halves always make one whole thing.

flyers-happen.hint: Ask 'What happened?' to find out about an event.
flyers-happen.fact: Stories often start by telling you what happened first.

flyers-hard.definition: difficult to do, or firm and solid
flyers-hard.hint: Some maths questions can be quite hard.
flyers-hard.fact: 'Hard' can mean difficult, or it can mean not soft.

flyers-hate.hint: Say 'I hate' only about things, not people, to be kind.

flyers-hear.definition: to notice a sound with your ears
flyers-hear.hint: You hear music with your ears.
flyers-hear.fact: Bats can hear sounds that humans cannot hear at all.

flyers-heavy.hint: A heavy bag is hard to carry far.

flyers-high.definition: a long way up from the ground
flyers-high.hint: Birds can fly very high in the sky.

flyers-hill.definition: a high area of land, smaller than a mountain
flyers-hill.hint: It's fun to roll down a grassy hill.
flyers-hill.fact: A hill is like a small mountain.

flyers-history.definition: the school subject about things that happened long ago
flyers-history.hint: In history class, we learn about people from the past.
flyers-history.fact: History helps us understand how the world became what it is today.

flyers-hole.definition: an empty space or opening in something
flyers-hole.hint: Rabbits dig a hole to make their home.
flyers-hole.fact: Golfers try to hit the ball into a small hole.

flyers-honey.definition: a sweet, sticky food made by bees
flyers-honey.hint: Bears love to eat honey from a beehive.
flyers-honey.fact: Bees make honey from the nectar of flowers.

flyers-hope.definition: to want something to happen and think it might
flyers-hope.hint: Say 'I hope it doesn't rain' before a picnic.
flyers-hope.fact: Hoping for good things can make you feel happy inside.

flyers-horrible.hint: A horrible smell makes you want to hold your nose.
flyers-horrible.fact: 'Horrible' is a strong way to say something is bad.

flyers-hotel.definition: a building where people pay to stay the night
flyers-hotel.hint: Families often stay in a hotel when they travel.
flyers-hotel.fact: Some hotels even have swimming pools for guests.

flyers-hour.definition: a unit of time equal to sixty minutes
flyers-hour.hint: There are twenty-four hours in one day.
flyers-hour.fact: A short film usually lasts about one or two hours.

flyers-how-long.definition: used to ask about the amount of time something takes
flyers-how-long.hint: Ask 'How long is the film?' to find out its length.
flyers-how-long.fact: 'How long' can ask about time or about size too.

flyers-hurry.hint: Hurry up so you are not late for the bus!
flyers-hurry.fact: When you hurry, your heart beats a little faster.

flyers-husband.definition: the man someone is married to
flyers-husband.hint: A husband and wife are a married couple.
flyers-husband.fact: A woman's husband is part of her close family.

flyers-important.definition: very valuable or needing serious attention
flyers-important.hint: Listening carefully in class is important.
flyers-important.fact: Remembering important dates, like birthdays, makes people happy.

flyers-improve.definition: to become better, or make something better
flyers-improve.hint: Practising every day helps you improve at reading.
flyers-improve.fact: Everyone can improve a skill with enough practice.

flyers-information.hint: Books and the internet are full of useful information.
flyers-information.fact: Libraries are great places to find information for a project.

flyers-insect.definition: a small animal with six legs, like an ant or bee
flyers-insect.hint: Ants, bees, and butterflies are all insects.
flyers-insect.fact: Insects are the largest group of animals on Earth.

flyers-instead.hint: Have juice instead of soda if you want something healthier.

flyers-instrument.definition: an object used to make music
flyers-instrument.hint: A piano, guitar, and drum are all instruments.
flyers-instrument.fact: Learning to play an instrument takes lots of practice.

flyers-interested.definition: wanting to know or learn more about something
flyers-interested.hint: Say 'I'm interested in space' to share what you enjoy.
flyers-interested.fact: Being interested in a topic makes learning much more fun.

flyers-interesting.definition: holding your attention because it is enjoyable to learn about
flyers-interesting.hint: A good book is often interesting from the very first page.
flyers-interesting.fact: Interesting facts are fun to share with friends.

flyers-invent.definition: to design or make something new for the first time
flyers-invent.hint: Thomas Edison helped invent the light bulb.
flyers-invent.fact: Children can invent new games with simple things at home.

flyers-invitation.definition: a card or message asking someone to an event
flyers-invitation.hint: You send an invitation to ask friends to your party.
flyers-invitation.fact: An invitation usually tells you the time, date, and place.

flyers-jam.definition: a sweet spread made from fruit and sugar
flyers-jam.hint: You spread jam on toast or bread.
flyers-jam.fact: Jam is made by cooking fruit with a lot of sugar.

flyers-job.definition: the work a person does to earn money
flyers-job.hint: Ask 'What job do you want?' to talk about the future.
flyers-job.fact: There are thousands of different jobs people can do.

flyers-join-a-club.definition: to become a member of a club or group
flyers-join-a-club.hint: You can join a club to make new friends with the same hobby.
flyers-join-a-club.fact: Joining a club is a fun way to try a new activity.

flyers-journalist.definition: a person who writes news stories
flyers-journalist.hint: A journalist asks questions and writes about what happens.
flyers-journalist.fact: Journalists work for newspapers, TV, and websites.

flyers-journey.definition: the act of travelling from one place to another
flyers-journey.hint: A journey can be short, like to school, or very long.
flyers-journey.fact: 'Journey' can describe a trip by car, plane, boat, or on foot.

flyers-just.definition: exactly, or only a moment ago
flyers-just.hint: Say 'I just finished' to mean you finished a moment ago.

flyers-keep.definition: to have or hold something and not give it away
flyers-keep.hint: You can keep your favourite drawing on your wall.
flyers-keep.fact: 'Keep' can also mean to continue doing something.

flyers-key.definition: a metal tool used to lock or unlock a door
flyers-key.hint: You need a key to open a locked door.
flyers-key.fact: The first metal keys were used thousands of years ago.

flyers-kilometre.definition: a unit used to measure distance
flyers-kilometre.hint: A kilometre is about the length of ten football pitches.
flyers-kilometre.fact: There are one thousand metres in one kilometre.

flyers-king.definition: a man who rules a country, often born into the role
flyers-king.hint: A king often wears a crown and lives in a palace.
flyers-king.fact: Some countries still have a king or queen today.

flyers-knee.definition: the joint in the middle of your leg
flyers-knee.hint: You bend your knee when you sit down.
flyers-knee.fact: Your knee helps you walk, run, and jump.

flyers-knife.definition: a tool with a sharp blade used for cutting
flyers-knife.hint: Always ask an adult before using a sharp knife.
flyers-knife.fact: A knife, fork, and spoon are the main tools we eat with.

flyers-land.definition: to come down and arrive on the ground after flying
flyers-land.hint: The plane will land at the airport soon.

flyers-language.definition: the words a group of people use to talk
flyers-language.hint: English is the language you are learning right now.
flyers-language.fact: There are thousands of different languages spoken around the world.

flyers-large.hint: An elephant is a very large animal.

flyers-late.definition: after the expected or usual time
flyers-late.hint: Set an alarm so you are not late for school.

flyers-later.hint: Say 'see you later' when you will meet again soon.
flyers-later.fact: 'Later' talks about the future, even if it's just in a few minutes.

flyers-lazy.definition: not wanting to work or be active
flyers-lazy.hint: It is easy to feel lazy on a rainy day.
flyers-lazy.fact: Even lazy days can be good for resting your body.

flyers-leave.definition: to go away from a place
flyers-leave.hint: We leave for school at eight o'clock.
flyers-leave.fact: 'Leave' can also mean to not take something with you.

flyers-left.definition: on the side opposite to the right
flyers-left.hint: Most people write with their right hand, but some use their left.

flyers-let.definition: to allow someone to do something
flyers-let.hint: Ask 'Please let me try' when you want a turn.
flyers-let.fact: 'Let's' is short for 'let us', used to suggest doing something.

flyers-lie.definition: to rest flat on a surface, like a bed
flyers-lie.hint: You lie down on your bed when you are tired.
flyers-lie.fact: 'Lie' can also mean to say something that is not true.

flyers-lift-ride.definition: a machine that carries people up or down in a building
flyers-lift-ride.hint: Take the lift instead of the stairs to a high floor.
flyers-lift-ride.fact: In American English, a lift is usually called an 'elevator'.

flyers-light.definition: not heavy, or having a lot of brightness

flyers-look-after.definition: to take care of someone or something
flyers-look-after.hint: You look after a pet by feeding it every day.
flyers-look-after.fact: Looking after younger children shows kindness and responsibility.

flyers-look-like.definition: to have a similar appearance to someone or something
flyers-look-like.hint: Say 'she looks like her mother' to compare appearances.
flyers-look-like.fact: Twins often look exactly like each other.

flyers-lovely.hint: Say 'what a lovely day' when the weather is nice.
flyers-lovely.fact: 'Lovely' is a warm, friendly way to say something is nice.

flyers-low.definition: not high, close to the ground
flyers-low.hint: The ball rolled under the low table.

flyers-lucky.definition: having good things happen by chance
flyers-lucky.hint: Say 'you're so lucky!' when a good surprise happens.
flyers-lucky.fact: Some people think a four-leaf clover brings good luck.

flyers-magazine.definition: a thin book with stories and pictures, published often
flyers-magazine.hint: You can read a magazine about animals or sport.
flyers-magazine.fact: New magazines come out every week or every month.

flyers-make-sure.definition: to check that something is definitely true or done
flyers-make-sure.hint: Make sure you have your bag before you leave.
flyers-make-sure.fact: 'Make sure' helps you avoid making silly mistakes.

flyers-manager.definition: a person who is in charge of a business or team
flyers-manager.hint: A shop manager makes sure everything runs smoothly.
flyers-manager.fact: A football team also has a manager who plans their games.

flyers-married.definition: joined to someone as husband and wife
flyers-married.hint: Married people often wear a ring on their finger.
flyers-married.fact: A wedding is the special day when two people get married.

flyers-match-football.definition: a game of football played between two teams
flyers-match-football.hint: Two teams play against each other in a football match.
flyers-match-football.fact: A football match usually lasts ninety minutes.

flyers-maths.definition: the school subject about numbers and shapes
flyers-maths.hint: In maths, you learn to add, subtract, and count.

flyers-may.definition: used to ask for or give permission
flyers-may.hint: Say 'May I go, please?' to ask politely.
flyers-may.fact: 'May' is a polite word for asking permission.

flyers-meal.definition: the food eaten at a certain time, like lunch
flyers-meal.hint: Breakfast, lunch, and dinner are all meals.
flyers-meal.fact: Many families enjoy eating a meal together.

flyers-mechanic.definition: a person who repairs machines, especially cars
flyers-mechanic.hint: A mechanic fixes cars when they stop working.
flyers-mechanic.fact: Mechanics use special tools to find and fix problems.

flyers-medicine.definition: something you take to help you feel better when ill
flyers-medicine.hint: A doctor tells you what medicine to take when you are sick.
flyers-medicine.fact: Some medicine comes as a tablet, and some as a liquid.

flyers-meet.hint: Say 'nice to meet you' when you meet someone new.
flyers-meet.fact: You might meet a new friend on your first day of school.

flyers-meeting.definition: when people come together to talk about something
flyers-meeting.hint: Grown-ups often have a meeting at work to make plans.
flyers-meeting.fact: Meetings help people share ideas and make decisions together.

flyers-member.definition: a person who belongs to a group or club
flyers-member.hint: Every member of the club gets a special badge.
flyers-member.fact: You become a member when you officially join a group.

flyers-metal.definition: made from a hard, shiny material like iron or gold
flyers-metal.hint: A metal spoon feels cold and hard.
flyers-metal.fact: Metal can be melted and shaped into many different things.

flyers-midday.definition: twelve o'clock in the middle of the day
flyers-midday.hint: The sun is highest in the sky at midday.

flyers-middle.definition: the point in the centre of something
flyers-middle.hint: Sit in the middle of the row to see the whole board.
flyers-middle.fact: Wednesday is right in the middle of the school week.

flyers-midnight.definition: twelve o'clock in the middle of the night
flyers-midnight.hint: Some people stay up until midnight on New Year's Eve.
flyers-midnight.fact: Midnight is the very start of a brand new day.

flyers-might.definition: used to say something is possibly true or could happen
flyers-might.hint: Say 'it might rain' when you are not sure about the weather.

flyers-million.hint: A million is a thousand thousands.
flyers-million.fact: If you counted to a million, it would take many days!

flyers-mind.definition: to feel bothered or upset by something
flyers-mind.hint: Ask 'Do you mind if I sit here?' to be polite.
flyers-mind.fact: 'I don't mind' means you are happy either way.

flyers-minute.definition: a unit of time equal to sixty seconds
flyers-minute.hint: There are sixty minutes in one hour.
flyers-minute.fact: It only takes a minute to brush your teeth!

flyers-missing.definition: not in the place where it should be
flyers-missing.hint: Look under the bed for your missing sock.
flyers-missing.fact: Posters sometimes ask for help finding a missing pet.

flyers-mix.hint: Mix blue and yellow paint to make green.
flyers-mix.fact: You mix flour, eggs, and sugar to make a cake.

flyers-money.definition: coins and notes used to buy things
flyers-money.hint: You need money to buy things at a shop.
flyers-money.fact: Money can be coins, paper notes, or even numbers on a card.

flyers-month.definition: one of the twelve parts of a year
flyers-month.hint: There are twelve months in a year.
flyers-month.fact: February is the shortest month of the year.

flyers-motorway.definition: a wide road for cars to travel fast between cities
flyers-motorway.hint: Cars drive fast on a motorway between towns.
flyers-motorway.fact: Motorways usually have several lanes for traffic.

flyers-much.definition: used to ask about or describe a large amount
flyers-much.hint: Ask 'How much does it cost?' when shopping.
flyers-much.fact: 'Much' is usually used with things you cannot count, like water.

flyers-museum.definition: a building where old and interesting objects are shown
flyers-museum.hint: You can see dinosaur bones in a museum.
flyers-museum.fact: Some museums keep objects that are thousands of years old.
